title: The place where you live
subtitle: on the outskirts, rent a flat, a lift, a cottage, central heating
summary: Describe where your home is, what kind of building it is and what it is like inside.

lesson.heading: Location
lesson.text: The **location** is the place and position of something. If you live **on the outskirts of town**, you live on the edge of town, not in the **centre**. If you **move**, you change the place where you live.

examples.text: We live **on the outskirts of town**, and it's a very nice **location**.
We used to live in the centre, but we **moved** to our present flat when we had children.
There's more **space** for them to play and it has nice **views**.
examples.note: space = an area that is empty or not used; views = the things you can see from a place

lesson.heading: A flat
lesson.text: If you **rent** a flat, you pay money every week or month to use it, because it isn't yours. A **block of flats** is a building with a number of flats in it. The **lift** is the machine that takes people up or down a floor.

examples.text: We **rent** a flat on the second floor.
There's a family in the flat **downstairs**, and a young French couple **upstairs**, on the **top floor**.
examples.note: downstairs = on a lower level of a building

examples.text: It's a modern **block of flats**, although the **lift** is small.

examples.note: air conditioning = a system that keeps the air cool

lesson.heading: The floors of a building
rows: at street level; you go in through the front door
the floor above the ground floor
the highest floor in the building
a small outside area on the wall of a flat
the stairs outside, up to the front door

lesson.heading: flat or apartment?
lesson.text: **Flat** is more common in British English; **apartment** is used in American English but is becoming more common in British English too. Apartments are usually in large buildings; flats can be in a large building or part of a larger house.

examples.text: We rent a small **flat** near the station.
I love my **apartment**. It has big windows.

lesson.heading: A house in the country
lesson.text: If you **own** a house, you bought it and it is yours. A **cottage** is a small old attractive house, usually in the country. **Charming** means pleasant and attractive, and a house with **character** is interesting and unusual.

examples.text: It's a **charming** house and has lots of **character**.
Like many old buildings, it's quite **dark**.
examples.note: the opposite of dark is light

lesson.heading: Keeping warm
lesson.text: To **heat** a room means to make it warm or hot. **Central heating** is a system that heats a whole house. Old buildings are often difficult to heat.

examples.text: The cottage is quite difficult to **heat**.
It doesn't have **central heating**, so it's cold in winter.
It's a very big house, so it costs a lot of money to **heat** in the winter.

lesson.text: Own and rent are opposites: you own your home if you bought it, and you rent it if you pay someone else every month to live there.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: the place and position of something
the things you can see from a place
the quality of being interesting and unusual
the machine that takes you up a floor
a small old house in the country

exercises.prompt: Is this a positive or a negative feature of a home?
Our flat doesn't have air ___, so it's very hot in the summer.
exercises.explanation: Air conditioning is a system that keeps the air cool.

exercises.prompt: My old flat was very small, but this one has much more ___.
exercises.hint: (an area that is empty or not used)
exercises.explanation: Space = room to move or to put things.

exercises.prompt: We live on the ___ of town, but it's only a twenty-minute walk to the centre.
exercises.explanation: On the outskirts of town = on the edge of town.

exercises.prompt: The flat is on the third floor, but we can sit outside on the ___.
exercises.hint: (a small outside area on the wall)
exercises.explanation: A balcony is the small outside area you can sit on, high up in a block of flats.

exercises.prompt: It's a very big house, so it costs a lot of money to ___ in the winter.
exercises.explanation: Heat = make warm or hot. A system for the whole house is central heating.

exercises.prompt: The flat's in a great ___: it's near the centre of town but opposite a park and very quiet.
exercises.explanation: Location = the place and position of something.

exercises.prompt: I'm on the second floor. I usually use the stairs, but I take the ___ if I'm feeling lazy.
exercises.explanation: The lift is the machine that takes people up or down a floor.

exercises.prompt: I love my apartment. It has big windows, so it's nice and ___ inside.
exercises.explanation: Light is the opposite of dark. Big windows make a room light.

exercises.statement: If you rent a flat, the flat belongs to you.
exercises.explanation: If you rent a flat, you pay money every week or month to use it, because it isn't yours. If it belongs to you, you own it.

exercises.statement: A cottage is a small old attractive house, usually found in the country.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Cottages often have lots of character but no central heating.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to explain why the family changed home.
exercises.answer: We moved to our present flat when we had children.
exercises.explanation: Move = change the place where you live.
